name: Pennylane
governance_notes: Founders hold 'ADP Fondateurs' preference shares that guarantee 51% of voting rights regardless of dilution (per the company's statuts, updated to May 2026), and a 2023 amendment added a share-transfer lock-up until 31 Dec 2032. This protects founder control and discourages early secondary sales -- a reasonable structure for a lender to note but not a red flag. The FY2022 accounts received an unqualified audit opinion from SEFAC with no going-concern qualification.
notes: Scored from Pennylane's actual filed French statutory accounts (comptes sociaux) for FY2022, the company's own filing with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Cherbourg -- not press-reported figures. This is FY2022, i.e. roughly two years before the ~EUR60m/EUR115m ARR figures reported in the press for 2024/2025; the two data points are NOT on the same basis and are not combined in this scorecard. FY2022 chiffre d'affaires grew 156% (EUR1.53m to EUR3.92m) off a small base, funded by a large equity round that year (share premium rose from EUR33.4m to EUR85.0m) rather than by revenue -- which is exactly why the burn multiple pillar below scores poorly despite the strong growth and runway numbers: this was a heavy-investment growth-stage year, not a capital-efficient one. Later press reporting (Sifted, Maddyness, 2025-2026) describes the company as having reached near-profitability by 2025, which is a materially different risk profile from this FY2022 snapshot -- illustrating why a screening tool needs a dated, sourced snapshot rather than a vague 'current state' assumption.
data_notes: Gross margin is left blank because Pennylane's French GAAP statutory accounts (comptes sociaux) do not separately disclose a cost-of-revenue line distinct from operating expenses -- 'Autres achats et charges externes' (EUR14.4m) bundles R&D subcontracting, marketing and overhead together, so no defensible COGS figure could be isolated. Monthly net burn (EUR1.79m/month) is derived by dividing the FY2022 operating result (resultat d'exploitation, EUR-21.52m) by 12 -- a proxy, since the filing does not include a cash flow statement. Cash on hand (EUR48,291,281) and existing debt (EUR200,000, a bank loan unchanged between FY2021 and FY2022) are both taken directly from the balance sheet (bilan) as filed. Source: PENNYLANE - Comptes sociaux 2022, filed 28/10/2024, provided directly by the user.

name: Younited Financial
governance_notes: Closed a SPAC merger with Iris Financial in December 2024, becoming a listed group (Euronext Amsterdam/Paris/Frankfurt, ticker YOUNI) and redomiciling from the Cayman Islands to Luxembourg. Externally reported as dilutive to historical shareholders (~57% discount versus prior valuation, per startup-in-europe.com). The FY2024 consolidated financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion from KPMG Luxembourg with no going-concern qualification identified. Total equity actually rose to EUR238.5m (from EUR143.4m) because the SPAC capital increase (EUR159.5m) outpaced the net loss.
notes: Scored from the audited FY2024 consolidated IFRS financial statements (KPMG-audited, the primary source, not an aggregator). Revenue declined 7.0% YoY (EUR101.76m to EUR94.67m) -- a real but fairly modest decline, notably smaller than the 27% figure a Yahoo Finance data feed had suggested before the primary source was checked. The headline net loss worsened sharply from EUR(49.7)m to EUR(83.4)m, but roughly EUR61.6m of that swing is attributable to one-off, largely non-cash items tied to the SPAC transaction: a EUR29.9m listing expense and EUR31.7m of accelerated share-based payment recognition triggered by the cancellation of legacy incentive plans at closing. Stripped of those, core operating performance was closer to flat year over year. H1 2025 results (not scored here, outside the FY2024 filing) showed revenue up 48% YoY, suggesting the FY2024 dip was not the start of a sustained decline.
data_notes: Gross margin, monthly net burn, cash-on-hand-based runway, and leverage are intentionally left unscored (not merely undisclosed) for this company -- see excluded_pillars. Younited is a licensed, deposit-and-wholesale-funded consumer credit institution, not an equity-funded startup: its balance sheet (EUR832.7m in customer deposits, EUR60.6m in loans from financial institutions) is deliberately leveraged as its core funding model, so a 'debt-to-revenue' leverage score or a startup-style 'cash runway' calculated the way this tool does for other companies would be actively misleading rather than merely approximate. The right lens for a licensed lender is capital adequacy and liquidity coverage ratios, which are outside the scope of this tool. Source: Younited Financial S.A. Consolidated Financial Statements FY2024, provided directly by the user.

excluded_pillars.gross_margin: Not meaningful for a licensed lender: IFRS revenue here is net interest income plus fee income, not a software/product margin -- there is no comparable 'cost of revenue' line to net it against.
excluded_pillars.runway: Younited is funded by customer deposits and wholesale borrowing, not an equity cash pile being drawn down -- a 'months of runway' calculation would misrepresent how the business is actually funded.
excluded_pillars.burn_multiple: Same reason as runway: the FY2024 net loss was ~74% driven by one-off SPAC listing and share-based payment costs, not cash burn against growth, and the funding model isn't equity-burn-based.
excluded_pillars.leverage: The balance sheet (EUR832.7m deposits, EUR60.6m institutional borrowing) is leverage by design as a regulated credit institution, not incremental risk layered on an equity base -- the right lens is capital adequacy/liquidity ratios, not a debt-to-revenue score.

name: Made.com
governance_notes: CEO Philippe Chainieux stepped down abruptly in February 2022 citing personal reasons, seven months before the company's collapse. A post-mortem (flinder.co) specifically questioned how the board signed off a clean going-concern assessment only nine months before the company entered administration.
notes: Historical case study, screened as if at the August 2022 trading update -- before the actual outcome (administration, 9 Nov 2022; assets sold to Next for GBP3.4m) was known. FY2022 revenue is the midpoint of the company's own guided -15% to -30% gross sales decline (announced 16 Aug 2022) applied to FY2021 actual revenue of GBP371m; FY2022 audited actuals were never published because the company entered administration before year end. Monthly net burn of ~GBP5m/month is derived by dividing the guided FY2022 EBITDA loss (GBP50m-70m, midpoint GBP60m) by 12 -- it is a derived estimate from company guidance, not a directly disclosed cash burn figure, and will understate actual cash burn for an inventory-heavy retailer (working capital consumed cash beyond the EBITDA loss, which is exactly why net cash fell from GBP31.5m at H1 2022 close toward a guided GBP5m-30m by year end). Net new revenue is negative because revenue was contracting -- see the burn multiple pillar in the scorecard for how the tool handles that case rather than dividing by a negative number.
data_notes: FY2021 revenue (GBP371m) and gross margin (46.3%, down from 53.2% in FY2020) are from the company's own full-year results. H1 2022 net cash (GBP31.5m) and FY2022 EBITDA loss guidance (GBP50m-70m) are from the company's own 18 August 2022 trading update. Exact existing debt / inventory financing terms were not found in the sources reviewed and are left at 0 -- this means 'no evidence found', not 'confirmed debt-free'. See SOURCES.md.
